tasks.gr9-atomic-age-nuclear-power-t2: Topic: The Atomic Age and Nuclear Power. Cover the dropping of atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki in 1945, immediate and long-term casualties, development of nuclear technology for weapons and peaceful uses (power generation, medical applications, research), the nuclear arms race between USA and USSR with thousands of warheads, the doctrine of Mutually Assured Destruction (MAD), and the Cuban Missile Crisis of 1962 as the closest approach to nuclear war. Ask Grade 9 learners to explain the destructive power of nuclear weapons, describe the arms race, analyze MAD as a deterrence strategy, evaluate the risks and promises of nuclear technology, and discuss how nuclear anxiety shaped Cold War society.
tasks.gr9-usa-ussr-superpowers-t2: Topic: USA vs Soviet Union: Superpowers. Cover the ideological confrontation between democratic capitalism (USA) and communism (USSR), NATO and the Warsaw Pact as opposing military alliances, proxy wars in Korea (1950–1953), Vietnam (1964–1975), and Afghanistan (1979–1989), the strategy of deterrence and containment, espionage and intelligence competition, and support for opposing sides in regional conflicts. Ask Grade 9 learners to compare superpower ideologies and interests, explain why proxy wars were fought indirectly, describe Cold War alliances, analyze how the superpowers competed without direct war, and evaluate the human cost of proxy conflicts.
tasks.gr9-space-race-berlin-wall-t2: Topic: Space Race and Berlin Wall. Cover Soviet achievements (Sputnik 1957, Yuri Gagarin first human in space 1961), the American response and Kennedy's Moon landing pledge, the Berlin Wall built in 1961 dividing East and West Berlin as a symbol of the Iron Curtain, the Apollo 11 Moon landing on July 20, 1969, and the transformation of space exploration toward cooperation. Ask Grade 9 learners to explain the significance of early Soviet space achievements, describe Berlin's division, analyze the space race as Cold War competition, identify major milestones from Sputnik to the Moon, and evaluate how space exploration later became a vehicle for cooperation.
tasks.gr9-end-of-cold-war-t2: Topic: End of the Cold War. Cover Mikhail Gorbachev's rise to power in 1985 and his reform policies of Glasnost (openness) and Perestroika (restructuring), the fall of communist regimes in Eastern Europe (1989–1990), the fall of the Berlin Wall on November 9, 1989, the collapse of the Soviet Union on December 26, 1991, and the transition to a new international order. Ask Grade 9 learners to explain why the Soviet system could not sustain itself, analyze the role of Gorbachev's reforms, describe how communist regimes fell across Eastern Europe, evaluate the international response to Soviet collapse, and discuss the opportunities and challenges of the post–Cold War world.
